question: Despite the sovereign European cloud project Gaia-X having failed, the Commission recently approved EUR 1.2 billion in funding to advance the European cloud1. 1.
So as not to repeat past mistakes, what precise steps will the Commission take today to strengthen the continent’s digital sovereignty?

If the aim is to design infrastructure guaranteeing a robust, competitive and independent European cloud, ensuring data security and user confidentiality, what specific measures will be taken to ensure compliance with ethical and data protection standards, guaranteeing that the development of the European cloud fully respects users’ fundamental rights and offers a reliable alternative to international solutions?
Finally, what will the Commission do to encourage the widespread uptake of the European cloud by companies and public organisations, so as to help reduce dependence on non-European providers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.4.2024) As part of its Data Strategy1, the Commission undertakes measures to strengthen the EU’s technological sovereignty, including for cloud users to access a competitive market where services operate in line with EU rules, such as the Data Act2 that tackles unfair cloud market practices.

On the supply side, a key measure is the Important Project of Common European Interest on Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI-CIS), approved under state aid rules on 5 December 20233. The IPCEI-CIS authorises seven Member States to mobilise up to EUR 1.

2 billion in public funding to support 19 projects for research and development, and first industrial deployment of beyond state-of-the-art advanced cloud and edge distributed data processing technologies and related services. The IPCEI-CIS does not replicate existing service offerings by nonEuropean providers or shape a single European competitor.
Significant positive dissemination activities targeting the non-participating companies and final users throughout Europe are a key part of this IPCEI.

The Commission also recently launched the development of an open-source smart middleware platform (SIMPL4) that will federate and interconnect European cloud services, including data spaces and public organisations’ cloud resources, and will boost cloud uptake among small and medium enterprises.
